newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian stocks end cautious session weaker.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian stocks end cautious session weaker.

text.p: SPI futures cl 2436 -18 US 30yr 6.83
10yrbond futs 92.480 -0.115 Gold NY 353.55 Lon Fix 354.20
*Stocks ended down in cautious trade ahead of a speech by Fed chairman Alan Greenspan. Volume 337.9 million, value A$599.3 million, 1,109 stocks traded, 332 steady, 314 rises, 463 falls.
Some cautionary profit-taking in resource issues before a speech from Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan later on Tuesday saw the Australian share market drift to a lower close.
The key share barometer, the All Ordinaries index closed 13.9 points down at 2,430.3, near its intra-day low of 2,427.9.
The March share price index finished down 18 points at 2,436 and at a 5.7 point premium to the underlying index.
Early weakness was inspired by bellwether stock BHP which surprised the market late on Monday with a news of a temporary shutdown of a blast furnace at its Port Kembla steelworks.

"Local investors are always nervous about the possibility of big correction on Wall Street. Basically, every time Greenspan speaks the market holds its breath and that's what it did today," a Melbourne-based dealer said.
The dealer said turnover remained subdued, with most investors happy to wait on the sidelines without anticipating the direction of Greenspan's impact on U.S. markets tonight.

"The outlook for the Australian market is still reasonably positive in the medium term even if there is a correction on Wall Street, otherwise I think the volume of selling would have been greater today," he said.
The gold sector was the weakest of the resources after the price of gold resumed its fall back towards the US$350 level after a minor recovery in London and New York commodity markets on Friday.
Industrial issues faired better, with the bank sector buoyed by the sustained rise of Commonwealth Bank stock as market talk continued that the bank may pay a special dividend.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Options trade was boosted by larger than normal volumes in National Australia Bank and Commonwealth Bank.
Total options traded 66,016 (27,978).
Turnover in March SPI contracts 5,419 (6,636).
In other local markets, Australian bonds weakened markedly, reversing all the gains made on Monday, with the long end weakening most ahead of Greenspan's speech later today.
The yield on ten-year T-bonds closed at 7.45 percent, down 0.13 percentage points from its closing level on Friday.
The Australian dollar subsided to a softer close Tuesday as fledgling attempts to reverse its month-old downtrend fell victim to market indifference.
At 5.00 p.m. (0600 GMT), the unit was quoted at US$0.7774/79, after reaching an intra-day low of US$0.7768.
Short-term range Support Restnce RSI-14 MA-10 MA-20

Bellwether company's shares weighed down the market after the company said it would lose iron production due to a problem with one of its blast furnaces at its Port Kembla steelworks in New South Wales.
Major resource issues follow BHP lower despite firmer base metal prices on LME.
Major bank's shares buck negative trend as speculation continues that the bank could declare a special dividend.
Bank's shares rebounded after being sold down on Monday after it said one of its executive directors had been charged under the Financial Transactions Reports Act.
